note: The guard was exercised against hand-crafted adversarial fixtures in tests/fixtures/ — LLM-shaped responses that WOULD be false reconciliations if produced live. The live batch (before_guard.json) produced 0 false reconciliations, so this artifact intentionally uses synthetic worst-case model outputs to prove the guard has teeth.

records.description: Naive adversarial: LLM proposes actual_fee=113.82 (2% + 18% GST, a plausible-sounding number) on ORD-0006. Neither the settlement nor the LLM's proposed math balances. gross(4823.00) - fee_charged(96.46) = 4726.54, but settled is 4703.20 (settlement internally inconsistent). And gross(4823.00) - actual_fee(113.82) = 4709.18, also not equal to settled. Guard rejects on both counts.
records.guard_reason: FEE_VARIANCE rejected. Failures: settlement_internally_consistent (gross Rs.4823.00 - fee_charged Rs.96.46 = Rs.4726.54; settled Rs.4703.20; gap Rs.23.34; tolerance Rs.4.82) | llm_actual_fee_agrees_with_payout (LLM's actual_fee Rs.113.82 vs payout's fee_charged Rs.96.46; gap Rs.17.36; tolerance Rs.4.82)

checks.name: settlement_internally_consistent
checks.detail: gross Rs.4823.00 - fee_charged Rs.96.46 = Rs.4726.54; settled Rs.4703.20; gap Rs.23.34; tolerance Rs.4.82

checks.name: llm_actual_fee_agrees_with_payout
checks.detail: LLM's actual_fee Rs.113.82 vs payout's fee_charged Rs.96.46; gap Rs.17.36; tolerance Rs.4.82

records.description: LLM claims TIMING_WINDOW while there IS an in-window payout for this order. TIMING means 'settlement cleared outside this batch's window' — by definition there should be zero in-window payouts. Guard rejects because the presence of an in-window row contradicts the timing narrative; the discrepancy is about amounts, not timing.
records.guard_reason: TIMING_WINDOW rejected. Failures: no_in_window_payouts (1 in-window payout(s); TIMING_WINDOW requires zero — any in-window payout means the discrepancy is about amounts/splits, not timing)

checks.name: no_in_window_payouts
checks.detail: 1 in-window payout(s); TIMING_WINDOW requires zero — any in-window payout means the discrepancy is about amounts/splits, not timing

records.description: LLM claims SPLIT_PAYOUT and cites leg_payout_ids ['PYT-Z1', 'PYT-Z2'] that do not exist among the in-window payouts for this order. If the guard trusted the LLM's claim without cross-referencing the payout registry, it would happily 'reconcile' against nonexistent rows. Anchored on the ORD-0043 messy-split shape from the live batch.
records.guard_reason: SPLIT_PAYOUT rejected. Failures: all_legs_exist_and_in_window (claimed leg IDs ['PYT-Z1', 'PYT-Z2'] vs in-window payouts ['PYT-0043A', 'PYT-0043B']; missing/unknown: ['PYT-Z1', 'PYT-Z2'])

checks.name: all_legs_exist_and_in_window
checks.detail: claimed leg IDs ['PYT-Z1', 'PYT-Z2'] vs in-window payouts ['PYT-0043A', 'PYT-0043B']; missing/unknown: ['PYT-Z1', 'PYT-Z2']

records.description: Ledger.status IS 'partially_refunded' — so the status check passes. But the LLM's proposed refund_amount does not close the arithmetic against the payout's actual fee_charged. gross(5000.00) - fee_charged(118.00) - refund(150.00) = 4732.00, but settled is 4700.00; gap Rs.32.00 > tolerance Rs.5.00. Guard rejects on the arithmetic. Shows that a correct-status classification still has to survive the numerical check.
records.guard_reason: PARTIAL_REFUND rejected. Failures: refund_arithmetic_closes (gross Rs.5000.00 - fee_charged Rs.118.00 - refund Rs.150.00 = Rs.4732.00; settled Rs.4700.00; gap Rs.32.00; tolerance Rs.5.00)

checks.name: refund_arithmetic_closes
checks.detail: gross Rs.5000.00 - fee_charged Rs.118.00 - refund Rs.150.00 = Rs.4732.00; settled Rs.4700.00; gap Rs.32.00; tolerance Rs.5.00

records.description: LLM proposes PARTIAL_REFUND with refund_amount=133.90 on ORD-0011 (from the live batch). The arithmetic works: gross(8945.00) - fee_charged(211.10) - refund(133.90) = 8600.00 = settled_amount. But ledger.status is 'captured', not 'partially_refunded'. Guard rejects because the ledger does not corroborate the refund event. This shows the guard cross-references ledger evidence beyond just arithmetic.

checks.name: refund_arithmetic_closes
checks.detail: gross Rs.8945.00 - fee_charged Rs.211.10 - refund Rs.133.90 = Rs.8600.00; settled Rs.8600.00; gap Rs.0.00; tolerance Rs.8.95

records.description: The 'smart lie.' LLM proposes actual_fee=119.80, which makes its own math perfect: gross(4823.00) - actual_fee(119.80) = 4703.20 = settled_amount. Guard rejects because 119.80 disagrees with the settlement row's actual fee_charged (96.46) by Rs.23.34, far outside the Rs.4.82 tolerance for a Rs.4823 gross. This is the pitch talking point: the guard validates against the settlement's own numbers, not against numbers the model produced. Anchored on ORD-0006 from the live batch.
records.guard_reason: FEE_VARIANCE rejected: the LLM's proposed actual_fee Rs.119.80 would arithmetically close the gap if used in place of fee_charged, but it disagrees with the payout row's actual fee_charged Rs.96.46 by Rs.23.34 (> tolerance Rs.4.82). The guard validates against the settlement's recorded fee, not the model's proposal.

checks.detail: gross Rs.4823.00 - fee_charged Rs.96.46 = Rs.4726.54; settled Rs.4703.20; gap Rs.23.34; tolerance Rs.4.82

checks.name: llm_actual_fee_agrees_with_payout
checks.detail: LLM's actual_fee Rs.119.80 vs payout's fee_charged Rs.96.46; gap Rs.23.34; tolerance Rs.4.82

records.description: LLM classifies as GENUINE_MISMATCH with reconciles=false — the honest 'I cannot reconcile this' verdict, matching what Gemini actually returned for ORD-0006 in the live batch. Guard accepts trivially because there is no claim to verify; the record is already escalated to human review.
records.guard_reason: LLM classified as GENUINE_MISMATCH; no claim to verify.

records.description: A genuine fee-variance case, matching the scenario the live batch injects for fee_variance orders. Merchant expected a flat 2% fee (Rs.20.00); aggregator charged 2% + GST (Rs.23.60). Settlement is internally consistent (gross - fee_charged = settled) and the LLM's proposed actual_fee agrees with the payout's fee_charged. Guard accepts.

records.description: A genuine split payout: two legs summing exactly to net_expected. Guard accepts because all cited leg IDs reference this order's in-window payouts and their settled_amount sums close to net_expected.
